name: mq_timedreceive
synopsis: ssize_t mq_receive(mqd_t mqdes, char *msg_ptr, size_t msg_len, unsigned int *msg_prio);
ssize_t mq_timedreceive(mqd_t mqdes, char *restrict msg_ptr, size_t msg_len, unsigned int *restrict msg_prio, const struct timespec *restrict abs_timeout);
description: mq_timedreceive() removes the oldest highest-priority message from a specified message queue and places it in a buffer, with an absolute timeout to prevent indefinite blocking if the queue is empty. It behaves like mq_receive() but returns immediately if the timeout expires.

parameters.name: msg_ptr
parameters.description: Pointer to the buffer to store the received message

parameters.name: msg_len
parameters.description: Size of the buffer pointed to by msg_ptr, must be at least the queue's mq_msgsize attribute

parameters.name: msg_prio
parameters.description: Pointer to return the priority of the received message, or NULL if not needed

parameters.name: abs_timeout
parameters.description: Absolute timeout for the operation, specifying seconds and nanoseconds since the Epoch

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes in the received message
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, with errno set to indicate the error

errors.description: The queue was empty, and the O_NONBLOCK flag was set for the message queue description.
The descriptor specified in mqdes was invalid or not opened for reading.
The call was interrupted by a signal handler.
The call would have blocked, and abs_timeout was invalid.
msg_len was less than the mq_msgsize attribute of the message queue.
The call timed out before a message could be transferred.
